artists.biography:
Gruffydd Maredudd Bowen Rhys (born 18 July 1970 in Haverfordwest) is a Welsh musician, performing solo and with several bands, including Super Furry Animals who obtained mainstream success in the 1990s. He also most recently formed the electro-pop outfit Neon Neon with Boom Bip. Their album Stainless Style was nominated for the 2008 Nationwide Mercury Prize. He won the 2011 Welsh Music Prize for his album Hotel Shampoo.
He was educated at Ysgol Dyffryn Ogwen, Bethesda, Gwynedd, North Wales and was awarded a degree in art at Manchester Metropolitan University.

Rhys had a batch of new songs, but no record label: Chant's proposal provided the motivation to finish off the lyrics. Rhys swiftly put together a band from local musicians, comprising former Flaming Lips drummer Kliph Scurlock, pianist Osian Gwynedd and bassist Stephen Black. Over three days of recording in Bristol, the new songs were laid down live in the studio – a working method he'd been developing across the American Interior album and his soundtrack for Set Fire to the Stars. “I wanted to make a live-based record, very simple and straightforward.” “On the morning of the first recordings I had the worst migraine,” Rhys later said. “I left the building and threw up in the street. perplexity.description:
Babelsberg is the fifth solo studio album by Welsh musician Gruff Rhys, released in June 2018 on Rough Trade Records. Musically, the album blends alternative rock with lush orchestral arrangements, performed by the BBC National Orchestra of Wales under the direction of composer Stephen McNeff. The collaboration brings a timeless, cinematic quality to Rhys’s songwriting, drawing comparisons to classic artists like Scott Walker and Jimmy Webb. The album’s sound is both grand and intimate, balancing melancholic themes with moments of romanticism and hope.

Within Rhys’s discography, Babelsberg stands out as his first album for Rough Trade and marks a shift toward more orchestral and conceptually ambitious work. While previous albums explored personal and historical narratives, Babelsberg addresses broader global concerns, including Brexit and social alienation, with lyrics that reflect both anxiety and resilience. The album received strong critical acclaim, earning an 82/100 on Metacritic and a 7.8/10 on AnyDecentMusic?, with reviewers praising its emotional depth and sophisticated arrangements. Though not a major commercial hit, Babelsberg is regarded as one of Rhys’s most accomplished and cohesive works.
